column3: “Observe” is rendered “celebrate.”
“Taken counsel” is rendered “decided,” and “officials” as “princes.”
“To what was sufficiency” is rendered “in sufficient numbers.”
“Pleasing” is rendered “right.”
“Appointed a word” is rendered “established a decree.” “Not to multitude” is rendered “not … in great numbers”; the phrase may also mean “not for a long time,” and the meaning is uncertain.
“The runners” is rendered “the couriers,” and “the escaped remnant which remains” as “those of you who escaped and are left.”
NASB supplies “so that.”
“Harden your neck” is rendered “stiffen your neck,” and “give a hand” as “yield.”
NASB supplies “will find” and “will return.”
“The runners” is rendered “the couriers”; “laughing on them” is rendered “laughed them to scorn.”
NASB supplies “some.”
“The command of the king” is rendered “what the king … commanded,” and “officials” as “princes.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Wadi” is rendered “brook.”
“The passover” is rendered “the Passover lambs”; NASB supplies “of themselves.”
“Place” is rendered “stations”; NASB supplies “which they received.”
“Passovers” is rendered “Passover lambs,” and “every not clean” as “everyone who was unclean.”
“With not according to what is written” is rendered “otherwise than prescribed”; NASB supplies “yet.” “Make atonement” is rendered “pardon.”
“Directed” is rendered “prepares”; NASB supplies “rules” and “though.”
“Listened” is rendered “heard.”
“A day in a day” is rendered “day after day,” and “instruments of strength” as “loud instruments.”

“Spoke to the heart of” is rendered “spoke encouragingly to,” and “understanding understanding good” as “showed good insight.” “They ate the appointed feast seven days” is rendered “they ate for the appointed seven days.”
“Took counsel” is rendered “decided”; NASB supplies “the feast.”

NASB supplies “there was nothing.”
“The priests the Levites” is rendered “the Levitical priests”; “the dwelling of his holiness” is rendered “His holy dwelling place.”
